title: Buying a Home in India: Document Checklist, Home Loan Basics and Vastu Tips
intro: A home is the biggest purchase most families make. Alongside traditional Vastu preferences, the legal papers and the loan numbers deserve the most attention. Here is a simple checklist.

p: Sale deed and the earlier link documents showing who owned the property before.
Encumbrance certificate (EC) to confirm there are no registered loans or disputes on the property.
Property tax receipts and utility bills with no dues.
Check that the project is registered with your state RERA and that approvals from the local planning authority are in place.
For a completed building, ask for the occupancy certificate.
A common guideline is to keep the total EMI at roughly 40 percent or less of your monthly income.
Compare interest rate, processing fee and prepayment rules across a few banks, and ask about loan insurance.
Traditional Vastu beliefs favour a main entrance facing east or north, the puja room in the north east, the kitchen in the south east and the master bedroom in the south west.
These are traditional beliefs. Never skip legal checks because a house looks good on Vastu.
Have a lawyer you trust review the papers. Do not hurry into paying a large advance. After the purchase, a griha pravesham at an auspicious time is a lovely way to begin.

faq.a: The sale deed, the link documents and the encumbrance certificate together prove ownership and a clean title.
It is a belief system. Legal clarity comes first, Vastu is a personal choice.

disclaimer: Note: general information only, not legal or financial advice. Please consult a lawyer and a financial adviser.
